title: Investigation of muscle spindles, receptors and nerve endings of human extrinsian eye muscles in patients with strabismus.
summary:
It has not yet been possible to prove whether and how a person can become aware of the position of the eyes in relation to the head and the environment. For the perception of the eye position, receptors and/or special nerve endings must be detectable in the eye muscles. In the muscles of the body, so-called muscle spindles and so-called Golgi tendon organs could be detected for the purpose of position perception. In the eye muscles muscle spindles are detectable, but not Golgi tendon organs. If the muscle spindles are used as receptors of the eye position, changes in muscle spindles could be detectable in squinting patients. Therefore, the tissue pieces obtained during standard squinting operations by muscle shortening are to be examined. The interested patient group consists of patients with an inner squint and patients with an outer squint.
We suspect that changes in the number, structure and size of muscle spindles of the eye muscles can be detected in squinting study participants. With our study, we want to expand our knowledge of squinting diseases and improve the treatment options for strabismus.

interventions.name: In patients with convergent strabismus or divergent strabismus, the possibly resected muscle-tendon pieces are examined as part of standard squinting operations. The tissue samples are examined using histological, immunohistological and electron microscopic methods.
